items.title: Karl-Anthony Towns Doesn't Expect To Sign Extension Before Regular Season
items.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns does not anticipate signing a contract extension with the New York Knicks before the regular season begins. Towns addressed the stalled talks Monday morning after a shootaround in Philadelphia. "It don't look good," said Towns. Towns is eligible to sign up to a four-year, $276 million extension. Towns holds a $61 million player option for next season. The gap between the sides is wide with New York's offer in the $45 million to $50 million per year range. The Knicks are near the second apron, and owner James Dolan has publicly said he does not want to cross it under any circumstance. The Knicks also plan to give Jalen Brunson a max contract next summer. Keeping the core intact while staying under the second apron will require other players to accept less money. Towns said he is willing to take a discount, but he also wants compensation that reflects what he and the team have accomplished over the past two seasons. "Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," said Towns. "None of those things have come close to happening." Towns was asked whether he can separate basketball from business. "In my experience, you just approach the moments right now and let it go where it goes," said Towns. Towns was then asked if he expected an extension to come easily given the team's recent success. "No s-t, Sherlock," said Towns. Towns is represented by CAA, which was formerly run by Knicks lead executive Leon Rose.

items.title: Joel Embiid Says He Feels 'Pretty Good' Following Sixers' Scrimmage
items.summary: Joel Embiid said that he felt "pretty good, not bad" following the Philadelphia 76ers' annual intrasquad scrimmage on Saturday. Embiid, who played 38 games last season, came to training camp noticeably slimmed-down. LeBron James also noted Embiid's health during training camp. "The difference between '24 and now, he's just so much more healthier," James said. "He hasn't missed a practice. He's been in damn near everything that we've done. Pretty much. They've had to sit him out at times, even when he wanted to keep going." Embiid then discussed the variety in the Sixers' offense. "Guys are going to use their speed against people and try to score a quick basket, and if we don't have anything, I'm the trail guy," added Embiid. The Sixers begin their four-game preseason schedule on Monday against the Knicks.

items.title: Josh Hart To Play Through Finger Injury Rather Than Undergo Career-Ending Surgery
items.summary: New York Knicks wing Josh Hart has abandoned plans for surgery on his right ring finger and will play through the pain for the rest of his career. Hart said Thursday the injury now requires a full joint replacement, which would end his NBA career. Hart explained why the procedure is not an option. "You can't have the banging, repetitive (motion)," said Hart. "Grabbing a rebound, palming it, shooting, catching the ball, doing all that: You can't do that. So, if I did a joint replacement, then I wouldn't be able to play." The 31-year-old will keep protecting the finger with a splint or wrap whenever he plays. Hart wore a splint throughout the 2025-26 season. Hart first hurt the finger during the 2025 Eastern Conference finals against the Indiana Pacers. Hart had surgery that offseason but aggravated it while guarding Mikal Bridges in a team scrimmage. He had planned to undergo a second operation after last season. Doctors told him this summer that a joint replacement was needed instead. Hart said he will likely have the procedure after he retires. The injury, which also affected a nerve, causes ongoing discomfort. "Some days, it'll be good. Some days it'll hurt to catch the ball," said Hart. "It varies. I wish I could tell you when I wake up, what's gonna be good, what's gonna be bad. Some days it's good, like a regular functioning finger; and other days, it hurts to just close my hand, to make a fist." Hart still produced the most efficient shooting season of his career in 2025-26, making a career-best 41% of his 3-point attempts and posted a career-high effective field-goal percentage. Hart is eligible for an extension but said at media day he did not expect one to get done. Hart is owed $43.3 million over the next two seasons, including a $22.4 million team option for 2027-28.
